events.credibility_reason: Several F10 signals together: sole unaffiliated author self-publishing on a non-refereeing venue a full resolution of a decades-old landmark problem; vocabulary ('wave-point geometry', 'tension flow', 'wave-action conservation laws') foreign to topological graph theory with no mappable step; cites none of the planar-cover literature and misdates the conjecture; part of a rapid series of same-creator 'wave point geometry' records; no uptake in four months, and later work (Koizumi–Suzuki–Tamura, Jun 2026) still states the conjecture as open.

why: The conjecture is equivalent to K₁,₂,₂,₂ having no finite planar cover, so in-window work is partial. The Annor–Nikolayevsky–Payne fold<14 result dates to v1 (3 Nov 2023), before the snapshot; v2 restates the same result by fold number, so per F1 it stays pre-snapshot, and I scored it a bound (smallest possible counterexample fold). Negami's JMSJ theorem proves the 'only if' direction for the class of rotation-compatible covers: a case, digested by journal publication and by Koizumi–Suzuki–Tamura's independent re-proof; its date is year-only 2024, so after_snapshot is null. The ANP 'Three theorems' paper rules out classes of planar covers of K₁,₂,₂,₂ (wheel-neighbourhood covers, certain face-length configurations, non-4-connected minimal covers), which I read as restricting the class of covers, hence case rather than none. Briański–Davies–Tan and Hliněný's Klein-bottle note are analogues on other surfaces (variant); the 2008 emulator construction concerns emulators, not covers (variant). The Matsuoka Zenodo claim is set aside as not_credible. No event involves any AI system.
doubts: Two close calls. (1) Koizumi–Suzuki–Tamura re-proves a case already settled by Negami's 2024 paper; I scored it case because it does prove a restriction, but it adds no new case and could reasonably be scored none. (2) ANP 'Three theorems' could be read as mere structural constraints on a hypothetical counterexample (none) rather than settling a class of covers (case); the theorem wording in the record is partial. Negami 2024's earlier public version, if any, was not found; its content is secondhand via KST.
